questions: Can numerical decisions read the queue's actual immutable artifact-reference representation and reject missing or altered inputs?
Can a native builder continue for at least three slots without reinlining a growing research context or tool transcript, while preserving exact original bytes?
Can compatible claims reuse one acquisition while keeping separate reviewed decision criteria?

criteria: Both artifact-backed and legacy inline inputs give the same descriptive decision when original bytes and frozen hashes agree.
A missing input produces no conclusive finding; inconsistent pointers, hashes or source identity cannot yield a decision.
Full context and tool history remain hash-bound files, with an explicit delivery inventory; no omitted inline material is described as reviewed.
Initial builder bootstrap is at most 16000 UTF-8 bytes. Requests approaching the native window checkpoint before another provider admission.
A confirmed local context boundary preserves files and continues as a new recorded slot; unknown or in-flight provider outcomes are never replayed.
The real pinned native CLI and Docker pass a three-slot synthetic-provider check with large retained context and exact installed-state markers.
A local Postgres race produces one campaign, one job and one execution commitment for two compatible claims, with separate protocols and decisions.
controls: Existing immutable history identity, checkpoint, path, budget, admission and cleanup regressions remain enabled.
Different source/configuration/seed/metric/resource identities remain distinct acquisitions.
No production writes, actual model calls, new AWS resources or assessment resumption during local verification.
uncertainty: Pass/fail software assertions only. Synthetic provider answers do not validate model planning, paper conclusions, native Linux networking execution or production behavior.
